title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor Performance - LS / LT V8
meaning: ECM registered oil pressure sensor voltage inconsistent with engine speed and oil temperature. On GM Gen IV (5.3L/6.2L Vortec) and Gen V (LT1/L83/L86) engines, the tiny cylindrical mesh filter screen located directly underneath the oil pressure sensor becomes plugged with carbon/sludge, starving the sensor of actual oil pressure (GM Bulletin 10-06-01-008D).
symptoms: Check Engine Light on and dashboard 'Oil Pressure Low - Stop Engine' chime
Instrument cluster oil pressure gauge drops to 0 PSI or reads erratic 80 PSI pegged
No mechanical engine tapping or lifter noise present (when gauge is false reading)
inspectionSteps: Verify actual mechanical engine oil pressure immediately with a physical pressure gauge hooked to the oil filter bypass port (minimum 6 PSI at hot idle, 24 PSI at 2000 RPM) to rule out oil pump failure.
Remove oil pressure sensor at rear of intake manifold behind cylinder 7.
Use a pick tool to reach down into the threaded oil port and remove the small plastic mesh filter screen (VLOM screen).
Inspect screen for heavy carbon varnish, metal debris, or sludged blockage.
verifiedFixes: Clean or replace the small oil pressure sensor micro-screen filter underneath the sensor
Replace faulty Engine Oil Pressure Sensor with genuine GM/ACDelco unit
Perform engine oil and filter flush with OEM PF63/PF48 filter

title: Engine Oil Pressure Switch Circuit - Low Voltage
meaning: ECM detected electrical short to ground or open circuit on the engine oil pressure switch signal circuit wire.
symptoms: Check Engine Light illuminated
Oil pressure warning light on cluster illuminated continuously
Oil pressure readout reads maximum pegged or minimum flat
inspectionSteps: Inspect wiring pigtail connector at the rear of engine block for heat damage from exhaust manifold.
Measure reference voltage from ECM (approx. 5.0V on 3-wire sensors, 12V on switches).
Test switch continuity to engine ground.
verifiedFixes: Replace faulty GM oil pressure switch/sensor assembly
Repair melted or shorted sensor harness wiring near firewall/exhaust

title: Fuel Pump Control Module (FPCM) Requested MIL Illumination
meaning: The stand-alone Fuel Pump Control Module (FPCM) mounted under the rear chassis near the spare tire detected an internal fault or fuel pump driver error and requested the ECM to illuminate the Check Engine light.
symptoms: Check Engine Light on
Intermittent extended cranking before starting or crank-no-start
Engine sputtering or dying under load or when turning
Fuel gauge occasionally dropping to empty
inspectionSteps: Scan the FPCM directly for secondary diagnostic trouble codes (such as P0231, P023F, U0109).
Inspect FPCM module casing and multi-pin connector mounted on the rear frame rail above spare tire for road salt corrosion, cracked plastic, or water intrusion.
Test fuel pump duty cycle and fuel pressure sensor PID.
verifiedFixes: Replace corroded Fuel Pump Control Module (FPCM) and program with GM SPS calibration
Repair green-corroded wiring terminal pins in FPCM harness plug
Replace high-amperage in-tank fuel pump assembly if drawing excessive current

title: Evaporative Emission (EVAP) Vent Solenoid Control Circuit
meaning: ECM detected open circuit, short to voltage, or short to ground on the control circuit of the EVAP canister vent solenoid valve on Silverado, Tahoe, Suburban, Sierra, or Corvette.
symptoms: Check Engine Light on
No perceptible change in engine performance or driveability
Vehicle fails state emissions smog inspection
inspectionSteps: Inspect EVAP vent solenoid valve mounted near the spare tire / fuel tank for road dirt contamination and salt corrosion.
Disconnect vent solenoid connector and test for battery voltage (12V) on power feed wire with key on.
Command vent solenoid ON/OFF with bi-directional scan tool and check for distinct audible click.
verifiedFixes: Replace EVAP canister vent solenoid valve assembly with updated GM remote-breather kit
Repair broken chassis wiring harness near rear axle
Clean or replace fuel vapor canister

title: Engine Misfire Detected - Active Fuel Management (AFM) Cylinder Deactivation
meaning: ECM detected erratic crankshaft deceleration pulses indicating cylinder misfire. On GM 5.3L and 6.2L V8 engines equipped with AFM / DFM, collapsed hydraulic deactivation lifters or bent pushrods on cylinders 1, 4, 6, or 7 are a primary cause (TSB 21-NA-096).
symptoms: Flashing Check Engine Light under acceleration
Loud, rhythmic metallic ticking noise from cylinder head / valve cover
Rough engine vibration and shaking at idle
Stabilitrak / Traction Control service warning lights illuminated
inspectionSteps: Scan live misfire counters to identify specific failing cylinder (typically cylinder 1, 4, 6, or 7).
Remove valve cover and inspect rocker arm movement during manual engine rotation; check for stuck collapsed lifter with excessive valve lash play.
Remove pushrod and check on flat surface for curvature/bend.
Inspect VLOM (Valve Lifter Oil Manifold) solenoids for sticking.
verifiedFixes: Replace collapsed AFM/DFM hydraulic valve lifters, lifter plastic guide trays, and bent pushrods
Replace Valve Lifter Oil Manifold (VLOM) assembly
AFM/DFM hardware delete with non-AFM camshaft and lifters (common enthusiast fix)
